text: A reliable process records what it changed and how the result was verified.
A version number is useful only when its compatibility contract is documented.
An unavailable dependency should produce a clear error instead of silent success.
A reviewer needs enough context to reproduce a reported failure.
A small example can explain an interface more clearly than a long description.
Sensitive values should not appear in logs, command arguments, or screenshots.
A deadline makes a stalled request observable and bounded.
Separate data from instructions when processing untrusted messages.
A checksum detects accidental changes but does not establish who created a file.
A test fixture should be deterministic and independent of external services.
A safe default limits access until an explicit policy grants more capability.
A migration should preserve enough information to diagnose partial failure.
A stable identifier helps connect related records across system components.
An independent review can catch assumptions that implementation tests miss.
A network timeout should have a finite upper bound.
A reproducible release records both source revision and artifact digests.
A private key should be readable only by the process that needs it.
Human confirmation is meaningful only when the approved action is shown precisely.
A data set should document its scope, source, version, and known limitations.
A failed validation should stop the operation before it produces side effects.
A backup is useful when restoration has been tested, not merely when it exists.
A clear error should identify the failed check without exposing secret data.
An audit record should distinguish a proposal from an executed operation.
A rollout can be reversed more safely when changes are isolated and versioned.
A meaningful benchmark includes examples the system was not tuned against.
